original_record.title: Dragging the knob snaps to the nearest stop and fires an alignment haptic on each change
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Composer/EffortSlider.swift:801-818 DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0) - the first change sets dragX inside .spring(response: 0.22, dampingFraction: 0.8), later changes set it directly; nearestStop is taken and, when it differs from the index, the index is written and NSHapticFeedbackManager performs .alignment at .now; onEnded clears dragX inside .spring(response: 0.32, dampingFraction: 0.78)

original_record.preconditions: A slider with two or more stops.
original_record.action: The user presses anywhere on the track and drags.
original_record.expected_result: A press with no movement already acts, because the minimum distance is zero: pressed on the track away from the knob, the knob springs to the pointer; pressed on the knob (within its 24 px radius of its drawn centre), it lifts to 1.06x where it is and never slides sideways (OD-0090). The knob follows the pointer, clamped to the insets, keeping the grip's offset when it was pressed on the knob (the source's knob centres on the pointer), and the selected index is the nearest stop to the knob's centre by rounding, so it changes as the centre passes the midpoint between two stops (OD-0090; the source rounds the pointer's position, which is the same except for the grip's offset). On the press the knob springs (response 0.22, damping 0.8): it lifts to 1.06x always, and slides to the pointer when it was pressed on the track; on release it springs onto the nearest stop and back to 1x (response 0.32, damping 0.78). The springs are the locked page's physical spring (work/design/jewel-knob-locked/jewel-knob.html:447-452: stiffness (2 pi / response)^2, damping 4 pi z / response), integrated in steps of at most 4 ms; a drawn frame moves them by the time since the last drawn frame, at most 50 ms (:813), so after a stall the knob goes on from where it was; the knob's drawn centre may pass either end's stop by at most 3 px while it springs (:586). Each index change fires an alignment haptic.

original_record.title: Dragging the knob snaps to the nearest stop and fires an alignment haptic on each change
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Composer/EffortSlider.swift:801-818 DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0) - the first change sets dragX inside .spring(response: 0.22, dampingFraction: 0.8), later changes set it directly; nearestStop is taken and, when it differs from the index, the index is written and NSHapticFeedbackManager performs .alignment at .now; onEnded clears dragX inside .spring(response: 0.32, dampingFraction: 0.78)
DroppyCode/App/Views/Composer/EffortSlider.swift:833-836 nearestStop = min(count - 1, max(0, Int(((x - inset) / step).rounded())))
original_record.preconditions: A slider with two or more stops.
original_record.action: The user presses anywhere on the track and drags.
original_record.expected_result: A press with no movement already acts, because the minimum distance is zero: pressed on the track away from the knob, the knob springs to the pointer; pressed on the knob (within its 24 px radius of its drawn centre), it lifts to 1.06x where it is and never slides sideways (OD-0090). The knob follows the pointer, clamped to the insets, keeping the grip's offset when it was pressed on the knob (the source's knob centres on the pointer), and the selected index is the nearest stop to the knob's centre by rounding, so it changes as the centre passes the midpoint between two stops (OD-0090; the source rounds the pointer's position, which is the same except for the grip's offset). On the press the knob springs (response 0.22, damping 0.8): it lifts to 1.06x always, and slides to the pointer when it was pressed on the track; on release it springs onto the nearest stop and back to 1x (response 0.32, damping 0.78). The springs are the locked page's physical spring (work/design/jewel-knob-locked/jewel-knob.html:447-452: stiffness (2 pi / response)^2, damping 4 pi z / response), integrated in steps of at most 4 ms; a drawn frame moves them by the time since the last drawn frame, at most 50 ms (:813), so after a stall the knob goes on from where it was; the knob's drawn centre may pass either end's stop by at most 3 px while it springs (:586). Each index change fires an alignment haptic.
side_effects: Haptic feedback on each stop crossed
original_record.persistence: Through the binding, the thread's effort and the model preference.
original_record.cancellation: A cancelled gesture or a lost pointer capture releases the knob exactly as a release does: it springs onto the nearest stop and back to 1x (OD-0090; work/design/jewel-knob-locked/jewel-knob.html:556-557 pointerup, pointercancel and lostpointercapture all run the same release; the source leaves dragX set until the next gesture, with no cancellation handler).
original_record.windows_path: The springs are the locked page's, whose numbers are the source's (response 0.22 s, damping 0.8 held; 0.32 s, 0.78 released), applied as in expected_result; the drag keeps the grip's offset and rounds the knob's centre to the nearest stop (OD-0090). Haptics have no Windows equivalent and are dropped silently, never substituted with sound (port_impacts X8(e)).

original_record.title: Dragging the knob snaps to the nearest stop and fires an alignment haptic on each change
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Composer/EffortSlider.swift:801-818 DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0) - the first change sets dragX inside .spring(response: 0.22, dampingFraction: 0.8), later changes set it directly; nearestStop is taken and, when it differs from the index, the index is written and NSHapticFeedbackManager performs .alignment at .now; onEnded clears dragX inside .spring(response: 0.32, dampingFraction: 0.78)
DroppyCode/App/Views/Composer/EffortSlider.swift:833-836 nearestStop = min(count - 1, max(0, Int(((x - inset) / step).rounded())))
original_record.preconditions: A slider with two or more stops.
original_record.action: The user presses anywhere on the track and drags.
original_record.expected_result: A press with no movement already acts, because the minimum distance is zero: pressed on the track away from the knob, the knob springs to the pointer; pressed on the knob (within its 24 px radius of its drawn centre), it lifts to 1.06x where it is and never slides sideways (OD-0090). The knob follows the pointer, clamped to the insets, keeping the grip's offset when it was pressed on the knob (the source's knob centres on the pointer), and the selected index is the nearest stop to the knob's centre by rounding, so it changes as the centre passes the midpoint between two stops (OD-0090; the source rounds the pointer's position, which is the same except for the grip's offset). On the press the knob springs (response 0.22, damping 0.8): it lifts to 1.06x always, and slides to the pointer when it was pressed on the track; on release it springs onto the nearest stop and back to 1x (response 0.32, damping 0.78). The springs are the locked page's physical spring (work/design/jewel-knob-locked/jewel-knob.html:447-452: stiffness (2 pi / response)^2, damping 4 pi z / response), integrated in steps of at most 4 ms; a drawn frame moves them by the time since the last drawn frame, at most 50 ms (:813), so after a stall the knob goes on from where it was; the knob's drawn centre may pass either end's stop by at most 3 px while it springs (:586). Each index change fires an alignment haptic.
side_effects: Haptic feedback on each stop crossed
original_record.persistence: Through the binding, the thread's effort and the model preference.
original_record.cancellation: A cancelled gesture or a lost pointer capture releases the knob exactly as a release does: it springs onto the nearest stop and back to 1x (OD-0090; work/design/jewel-knob-locked/jewel-knob.html:556-557 pointerup, pointercancel and lostpointercapture all run the same release; the source leaves dragX set until the next gesture, with no cancellation handler).
original_record.windows_path: The springs are the locked page's, whose numbers are the source's (response 0.22 s, damping 0.8 held; 0.32 s, 0.78 released), applied as in expected_result; the drag keeps the grip's offset and rounds the knob's centre to the nearest stop (OD-0090). Haptics have no Windows equivalent and are dropped silently, never substituted with sound (port_impacts X8(e)).
original_record.verification_method: interaction test dragging across all stops
